findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: PepsiCo's July 'towards the low end' FY26 guide was set with Brent at $74.46 (2026-07-09) and an explicit plan that gas prices would come down in H2; Brent is $125.44 (2026-10-06), diesel $6.20 (2026-10-05, +25% vs July, about +67% YoY) and gasoline $4.35 (not down). The low end still needs roughly +8-9% core constant-currency EPS growth in the 16-week Q4 on top of +11% in Q4 2025, and FY26 consensus sits unrevised at the low end ($8.57 a month ago, $8.56 now). So a trim or an explicitly qualified guide is more likely than the consensus implies: I put about 38% on a formal cut below 4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cut Apr-2025 -4.89%; weak initial guide Feb-2025 -4.51%; reaffirmed 'towards the low end' Jul-2026 -3.26%; reaffirmed with Brent near $117 Apr-2026 +2.28%; reaffirmed Feb-2026 +4.93%, Oct-2025 +4.23%, Jul-2025 (with NA improvement) +7.45%. Baseline labels these 'amc' because the 8-K is accepted about 22:00 ET the evening before; the moves are the bmo reaction-day closes.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY26 EPS moved $8.57 -> $8.56 in 30 days (Nasdaq/Zacks: 3 analysts lowered, the mean moved $0.01) while Brent rose ~31% from 2026-09-01 and diesel ~14%; Q4 consensus still $2.43 (+7.5% YoY). PEP's excess return over XLP has ~0 correlation (+0.05, 60 sessions) with daily Brent moves since 2026-07-10, and PEP was +0.2% on 2026-10-02 when Brent rose 18%. If the cost hit were priced, Q4/FY estimates would sit below the low end and PEP would trade against oil relative to staples. The -9.3% 20-day fall matches packaged-food peers (GIS -14.1, CAG -12.2, CPB -13.8, KHC -10.8) rather than PEP-specific oil exposure. Biases: stale estimates and anchoring on the company's guide. Kept small and wide because the skew bids calls (-3.51 vol pts) and PEP rallied on 4 of its last 5 guide-affirming prints, so a hold is a relief rally.
findings.independence: RBC (2026-10-06) independently expects freight and logistics costs to pressure the December quarter and early 2027: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/pep-q3-preview-rbc-sees-145658271.html ; Conagra's CFO (2026-09-30) reported accelerating logistics inflation driven by oil: https://www.cfodive.com/news/conagra-cfo-cites-logistics-transportation-accelerating-inflation/831822/ ; PPI truckload trucking +13.9% YoY in Aug-2026: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=PCU484121484121. Against: General Mills (2026-09-23) and Conagra both reaffirmed (their fiscal years end in May, so they have more runway), and the Q2 10-Q shows $215M of net cash-flow-hedge gains to reclassify into income over the next 12 months: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/77476/000007747626000035/pep-20260613.htm

findings.finding: PFNA laps a -4% volume / -3% organic Q3 2025 (against -1% / -2% in Q2 2025). On the Q1 and Q2 2026 two-year volume stacks (about 0 and -1), PFNA volume should print about +1 to +2% with organic about -1%, and total organic about 3% against ~2.8% (JPM's revised estimate). But tracked channel data (JPM) and Couche-Tard say North America ran below plan, so the net is a small positive in how the release reads.

findings.why_not_priced: The comp is public, but the street has just cut organic estimates on channel data (JPM 3.2% -> 2.8%), which extrapolates Q2's -2% PFNA print. Previews call PFNA volume growth the 'must show' number (24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-07) rather than the expected one. If the comp were priced, the previews would treat volume growth as the base case.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-24 PepsiCo said it will raise chip and some soda prices by low-to-mid single digits 'in line with inflation' at the end of 2026 or early 2027, after 'higher commodity costs this year'.
